opus.why: Just a greeting. Any model handles it.

fable.why: Greeting with no task. Any model answers identically.

opus.why: A thank-you that needs only a short acknowledgment.

fable.why: Acknowledgement closing a thread; a one-line reply is all that is needed.

opus.why: A simple time-zone lookup that needs at most one tool call.

fable.why: Current time in Tokyo is a single command or lookup plus a timezone offset; no judgment involved.

opus.why: Find the test command, run it and report the results. No fixing was asked for.

fable.why: Find the test command, run it, report pass/fail faithfully. Medium so it does not stop early or skip reading the output; no reasoning beyond that.

opus.why: The deploy affects shared systems, so the model has to find the right process, check the state first and handle any failures carefully. Haiku might cut corners here.

fable.why: Deploy to staging is an outward-facing, hard-to-reverse action: must locate the right script or pipeline, check branch state, and react correctly if a step fails. Haiku is more likely to skip a check or pick the wrong target; Sonnet medium handles well-specified agentic tasks reliably.

opus.why: Routine git work plus a short commit message based on the diff. Medium effort makes it look at the changes before pushing.

fable.why: Read the diff, write a sensible commit message, commit and push. Routine git work; medium keeps it from skipping the diff read.

opus.why: Reads project notes or memory and summarizes the current task. Just retrieval.

fable.why: Read the project's notes or todo files and summarize what is pending. Retrieval and summary, no creative or brand output.

opus.why: Mechanical lint fixes: remove unused imports, change var/let to const, replace any and type the sleep parameter. A small file with clear fixes.

fable.why: The file is tiny and the lint issues are obvious: var to const, unused react import, implicit/explicit any, untyped ms parameter. Mechanical cleanup Haiku does correctly.

opus.why: Hooks are audience-facing creative copy where punch and originality matter, and the model has to infer the topic and brand voice from project context. Weaker models give generic hooks.

fable.why: Five reel hooks are final audience-facing copy where the first second decides retention. Needs to pull the studio project's brand voice and produce punchy, non-generic Russian hooks; this is where weaker models read as flat or clichéd, which the owner would notice.
